summary:
I reviewed the ui-widgets-theme scope with the frontend-design, clean-code-guard, code-complete and frontend-ui-engineering checklists. I read these files in full: operating_panel.rs, audio_card.rs, theme.rs, action_catalog.rs, action_shortcuts.rs, global_shortcuts.rs, persist.rs, background_io.rs, audio_presets.rs and operator_picker.rs. I skimmed the outlines of the other widgets (chart, volume_meter, deck_controls, scene_card, status_bar, studio_controls, transport_bar) and diffed resources/themes/*.css.

Main problems, worst first:

1. **operating_panel.rs is a whole page filed as a widget.** It is the Sources inspector (2361 lines, about 1613 production), and the 9-line src/ui/pages/sources.rs only forwards to it. `populate` is about 418 lines and `build_source_detail` about 394. It finds its own widgets again by walking the whole tree and matching names built with `format!`. Some of those names contain translated text, so they change with the locale.
2. **Rules that are not UI code live in ui/.** action_catalog.rs decides whether an operator action is allowed (`resolve_with_inputs`). action_shortcuts.rs owns shortcut conflict rules. audio_presets.rs owns preset validation and plan building. persist.rs owns the legacy-registry migration rule. global_shortcuts/portal.rs is a D-Bus client that touches no widgets.
3. **OBS request names leak into the UI as raw strings.** There are about 60 literals such as "SetInputMute", checked by three separate helpers (`supported`, `supports`, `capable`). The obs/ boundary should turn these into a typed value instead.
4. **persist.rs and background_io.rs each pile 4-5 jobs into one file**, held together by thread-local globals. Every background job polls on its own 20 ms timer, and there is production `.expect` (one in persist.rs, five lock expects in background_io.rs).
5. **theme.rs is less bad than its size suggests.** About 60% of its 1553 lines are tests. The production part still mixes the theme list, the custom-CSS security check, CSS provider handling and desktop integration. Adding a theme means editing four places.
6. **The charts and level meters hard-code their colours.** They ignore the theme tokens, so the High Contrast theme cannot reach them, and "good" is blue in charts but green everywhere else.
7. **Many dialogs redraw on a 250 ms or 1 s timer** instead of reacting to state changes.
8. **Small helpers are copied around.** A `text()` label builder exists in 7 files, and the app's page list exists in 3 places that disagree with each other.

The proposed splits keep the existing native GTK tests and unit tests as the safety net. Each split moves code without changing behaviour first. Pure logic (source drafts, the registry write journal, the action resolver, shortcut conflict checks, preset rules) comes out into units that can be tested without GTK. Replacing widget-name lookups with typed handles changes behaviour, so it is a separate later step.

What I did not check: I ran no tests or builds (the review was read-only), and I only scanned the remaining widget files rather than reading them line by line. Some of these findings depend on other reviewers' work: the AppState revision counter belongs to the window.rs/state.rs reviewer, and moving the portal client into infra/ needs a check against architecture_tests.rs.

VERIFIER: every finding re-checked against source at HEAD 31d512f. Findings: adjusted 11, confirmed 11. Key corrections: uiw-04/action_catalog split must not move resolve into src/domain (it reads storage SceneRegistry and controller RegistryStatus; architecture_tests would fail) - use src/controller/state/action_resolution.rs; uiw-05 OBS protocol names belong in obs/mapper.rs, not domain; uiw-11 volume meter colours are deliberately fixed (volume_meter.rs:60-64); uiw-08 lock-poison risk is near-unreachable and futures_util::channel needs a feature flag; uiw-13 domain type is SceneHotkeyConfig and ActionShortcut::conflict already exists; uiw-21 ids persist, so display-name renames need no aliases. No finding fully refuted.

findings.title: Sources page lives in widgets/ as a 2361-line god file with 400-line routines
findings.evidence: operating_panel::build is the entire Sources page (root CSS class 'sources-page' line 101; only caller src/ui/pages/sources.rs:8 is a 9-line shim plus lifetime_tests.rs:83). populate() spans 678-1096 (~418 lines: heading, status line, scene selector, source list, search, split view, breakpoint, detail). build_source_detail() spans 1098-1492 (~394 lines: filters, text editor, media, advanced audio). The build() refresh closure (162-252) mixes content diffing, focus capture, scroll restore and idle re-focus. Tests span 1614-2361.
findings.recommendation: Move to src/ui/pages/sources/ (see proposed_splits). Delete the shim src/ui/pages/sources.rs and drop `pub(crate) mod operating_panel` from src/ui/widgets/mod.rs:14. Split populate into browser.rs::build_browser(...) -> SourceBrowserHandle and detail/mod.rs::build_detail(...) -> DetailHandle. Split build_source_detail into one module per section: detail/filters.rs, detail/text_editor.rs, detail/media.rs, detail/audio.rs. Each section function stays under ~80 lines.
findings.risk: Any edit to Sources touches a 2.3k-line file. Merge conflicts and missed edge cases in the 400-line routines.
findings.smell: Large Class / Long Method / Divergent Change
findings.verifier_note: Verified: pages/sources.rs is a 9-line shim forwarding to operating_panel::build (line 8); root class 'sources-page' at 101; populate 678-1096, build_source_detail 1098-1492, tests from 1614. Other callers: widgets/lifetime_tests.rs:3,83 and widgets/mod.rs:14. Moving under ui/pages/ does not trip architecture_tests (pages_reach_the_controller_only_through_navigation forbids only `AppController`). Native test child names embed module paths and must be renamed on the move: operating_panel.rs:1620, 1760 and operating_panel/media_progress.rs:147.

findings.title: Widget-name string registry and full-tree visit() used as data binding (locale-dependent keys)
findings.evidence: Updates locate widgets by recomputing names: update_media_values compares widget_name to format!("control-focus-seek-position-{}", input) for every visited widget (279). update_observed_controls builds HashMaps keyed by format!("control-focus-item-{owner}-{item_id}-{path}") (372-376). update_detail_values keys spin buttons by format!("control-focus-number-{title}"), where title is the localized fl!("control-audio-sync") (430-450, matching add_numeric_apply 1541). expand() marks the media section by comparing its translated title: `if title == fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "control-media")` (1608). update_status walks the whole tree on every refresh and every 1 s tick (591-650).
findings.recommendation: Return typed handles at build time, as AudioCardHandle already does (audio_card.rs:42-53). Proposed shapes: `struct SourceRowHandle { check: CheckButton, hidden_parent: Label }` keyed by `SourceItemKey { owner, item_id, path }`. `struct DetailHandles { text: Option<TextEditorHandle>, media: Option<MediaHandle>, audio: Option<AudioHandle>, filters: HashMap<String, CheckButton> }`. `struct StatusHandles { loading, error, result, age, stale: Label, refresh: Button, split: NavigationSplitView }`. Keep widget names only as test and focus anchors, built from ids, never from translated text. Replace `expand(.., _expanded)` with `section(parent, title) -> GtkBox` and set the media marker at the call site.
findings.risk: In a locale where two labels translate the same, the widget-name keys collide. Each pass walks the whole tree and formats a string per widget. Renaming a translation can silently break updates.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: format!("control-focus-seek-position-{}") at 279; item/hidden-parent keys at 372-376; numeric keys built from fl!("control-audio-sync"/"control-audio-balance") at 430-450 and matched against add_numeric_apply's set_widget_name(format!("control-focus-number-{label}")) at 1541 (the apply button is also named from the label at 1544); expand() compares the translated title to fl!("control-media") at 1608. Locale collision itself is speculative (needs two identical translations); the real defect is that names derive from translated text. Note tests locate widgets by these names (e.g. named() helper ~1780), so the behaviour-changing step must keep id-based names as test anchors.

findings.title: Draft-editing state is an anemic struct whose maps are edited from outside with magic field keys
findings.evidence: LocalState mixes view flags (query, show_detail, usage_expanded, syncing) with draft state: text_drafts/text_origins, numeric_drafts: HashMap<(String,String),f64> keyed by the literals "seek"/"sync"/"balance", and track_drafts: HashMap<String,[bool;6]>. Callers reach into the maps directly: cancel does `local.borrow_mut().text_drafts.remove(&input)` and `text_origins.remove` (1231-1232). Seek does `numeric_drafts.remove(&(input.clone(), "seek".into()))` (1320-1321). Track toggles do `track_drafts.entry(input.clone()).or_insert(observed)[index] = ...` (1457-1461).
findings.recommendation: Create src/ui/pages/sources/drafts.rs with `enum NumericField { Seek, SyncOffset, Balance }` and `struct AudioTracks([bool; 6])`. Add `struct SourceDrafts` with intent methods: text_draft, edit_text, discard_text(input), text_conflict, numeric(input, field, observed), set_numeric_text, commit_numeric(input, field), tracks(input, observed), toggle_track(input, index, observed), reset_for_epoch(epoch). Keep view flags in a separate `SourcesViewState { query, show_detail, usage_expanded }`. Make the fields private. Move the unit tests at 2275-2345 next to it and add one test per NumericField.
findings.risk: Draft invariants (origin tracking for conflict detection) can be broken by any call site that forgets to clear the paired map.
findings.smell: Data Clumps / Primitive Obsession / Inappropriate Intimacy
findings.verifier_note: Verified: LocalState 17-29 mixes view flags with drafts; external map edits at 1231-1232 (text_drafts/text_origins), 1320-1321 (numeric_drafts and numeric_text keyed by (input, "seek")), 1457-1461 (track_drafts.entry). Add numeric_text to SourceDrafts too (reviewer omitted it). Unit tests at 2276-2345 exist as cited.

findings.title: Operator-action permission rules (resolve/observed_label) live in ui/ and repeat the target match three times
findings.evidence: resolve_with_inputs (158-287) decides whether a pinned or shortcut action may run. It checks connection, scope, registry readiness, scene role is_live_switchable, freshness via can_control, capability and ambiguous identity. It has no GTK at all and only reads AppState. observed_label (66-145) is the same rule pattern returning localized strings. The OperatorAction to ActionTarget match is written three times (99-104, 207-215, 647-655). action_shortcuts.rs, global_shortcuts.rs, operator_picker.rs and quick actions all reach this rule set through ui::action_catalog.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add `impl OperatorAction { pub fn target(&self) -> Option<&ActionTarget> }` in src/domain/operator_action.rs and replace the three matches. (2) Move the rules into src/domain/operator_action/resolution.rs: `pub enum ResolvedAction { Control(ControlAction), OpenSource(String) }`, `pub fn resolve(ctx: &ActionContext<'_>, action: &OperatorAction) -> Option<ResolvedAction>`, and `pub fn observed_state(ctx, action) -> Option<ObservedActionState>`, where ObservedActionState is an enum (Active/Inactive/Program/Preview/Ready/Muted/Unmuted/FilterOn/FilterOff/Media(MediaState)) and the UI maps it to fl! keys. (3) Build `ActionContext<'a>` (borrowed scenes, registry roles, inputs, audio, operator_inputs, capabilities, readiness flags) via `AppState::action_context()` in a new src/controller/state/action_context.rs, not in the already-huge state.rs. (4) Leave entries/binding_entries/execute in ui/action_catalog/.
findings.risk: The safety rule that decides whether a live action may run is hard to find and is bound to the UI module. Other front ends (hotkeys, a future CLI) would copy it.
findings.smell: Feature Envy / Misplaced Responsibility / Duplicate Code
findings.verifier_note: Rules are GTK-free (confirmed, 158-287 and 66-145). Two corrections. (1) The three matches are NOT identical: 99-104 and 207-215 list OpenSource/SetMuted/ToggleMuted/RestartMedia/SetFilterEnabled/ToggleFilter (no Scene); 647-655 lists Scene but not OpenSource. So OperatorAction::target() must return the target for every target-carrying variant and each call site keeps its own variant filter; it is not a drop-in replacement. (2) Moving resolve into src/domain/ would break architecture_tests::domain_and_services_do_not_reach_into_storage and the domain-depends-on-nothing rule: resolve reads state.registry (crate::storage::registry::SceneRegistry, controller/state.rs:16,454), state.show_registry.status (controller::state::RegistryStatus, controller/state/show_registry.rs:11) and WorkspaceState (controller). Corrected recommendation: put the rule in src/controller/state/action_resolution.rs as `impl AppState { pub(crate) fn resolve_action(&self, action) -> Option<ResolvedAction>; pub(crate) fn observed_action_state(&self, action) -> Option<ObservedActionState> }` (controller may use storage+domain and has no GTK). Only the pure enums ResolvedAction/ObservedActionState go in src/domain/operator_action.rs. A domain-level ActionContext is only viable if every field is flattened to domain types/bools; do not borrow SceneRegistry/RegistryStatus there.

findings.title: Raw OBS protocol request names spread through the UI with three different capability helpers
findings.evidence: About 60 literal OBS request names in ui (non-test): operating_panel.rs 22 (e.g. "SetSceneItemEnabled" 816, "SetInputAudioTracks" 1471), action_catalog.rs 14, transport_bar.rs 11, studio_controls.rs 6, audio_presets.rs 6. They are checked by three look-alike helpers: operating_panel::supported(caps: &[String], &str), transport_bar::supports(&AppState, &str) and audio_presets::capable (an array .all()), plus a closure in action_catalog:168. AppState.available_requests is Vec<String> (controller/state.rs:447).
findings.recommendation: Add src/domain/obs_capability.rs with `pub enum ObsCapability { SetSceneItemEnabled, SetSourceFilterEnabled, SetInputSettings, TriggerMediaInputAction, SetMediaInputCursor, SetInputAudioMonitorType, SetInputAudioSyncOffset, SetInputAudioBalance, SetInputAudioTracks, SetInputMute, SetInputVolume, SaveReplayBuffer, SetCurrentPreviewScene, SetCurrentProgramScene, ... }` and `pub struct CapabilitySet(BTreeSet<ObsCapability>)` with `supports(cap)` and `supports_all(&[cap])`. src/obs/mapper.rs converts the OBS request-name list into a CapabilitySet (unknown names are dropped). Change AppState.available_requests to CapabilitySet. Delete the three helpers. Add a domain test that round-trips every variant's protocol name.
findings.risk: OBS vocabulary bypasses the obs/ boundary. A typo in a literal silently disables a control. Shotgun Surgery when OBS renames a request.
findings.smell: Primitive Obsession / Shotgun Surgery / Duplicate Code
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed in substance: AppState.available_requests: Vec<String> (controller/state.rs:447), helpers operating_panel::supported (1560), transport_bar::supports (219), audio_presets::capable (118-134), closure action_catalog:168. Also missed: studio_controls.rs:214 closure and previews.rs:84 inline scan, so 5+ copies. A grep for Set*/Save*/Trigger* literals finds ~46 non-test hits (21 operating_panel, 14 action_catalog, 5 studio_controls...); Start*/Stop*/Get* bring it near the claimed ~60. Corrections: (a) protocol strings are OBS vocabulary, so the variant<->"SetInputMute" mapping must live in src/obs/mapper.rs (ACL), with the round-trip test in obs/, and src/domain/obs_capability.rs holds only the enum + CapabilitySet with no protocol names. (b) The raw list also flows through controller/event.rs:16 and is built in fixtures (app.rs:555, session_reports.rs:490, bookmarks.rs:464); before dropping unknown names, check whether session reports/diagnostics display the raw list - if so keep a separate raw Vec for reports. Unverified: whether any Doctor check reads available_requests.

findings.title: persist.rs mixes a write journal, an import transaction gate, scope selection with migration policy, i18n messages and config saves
findings.evidence: (a) A registry write journal state machine (RegistryWrites, confirm_*, registry_write_finished, submit_registry_write_to, retry_registry_writes; 23-205) held in a thread_local. (b) An import gate with RAII guard and deferred job queue (REGISTRY_IMPORTING, AFTER_REGISTRY_IMPORT, RegistryImportGuard, begin_registry_import; 207-271) plus import_registry_to_target (416-455). (c) Presentation: registry_availability_message returns fl! strings (273-287). (d) select_registry_scope (291-354) contains the legacy-registry migration rule: compare config.legacy_registry_endpoint (or host:port) with key.endpoint and key.connection == "default" (318-328). (e) Config persistence (463-497). There is a production panic at 317: `begin_registry_import().expect("deferred registry jobs run outside the gate")`.
findings.recommendation: Split into src/ui/persist/ (see proposed_splits). Move the legacy-source decision into storage as `RegistryTarget::legacy_source(&self, config: &AppConfig) -> Option<PathBuf>` in src/storage/show_workspaces.rs, unit-tested there. Move registry_availability_message to src/ui/registry_status.rs. Replace the .expect at 317 with `let Some(guard) = begin_registry_import() else { tracing::error!(...); failed finish_registry_load(...); return; }`.
findings.risk: Five reasons to change one file. The migration rule sits in a GTK callback, and a broken gate invariant panics the GTK thread.
findings.smell: Divergent Change / Large Class / Global State
findings.verifier_note: Verified: journal 23-205 with thread_local at 42, import gate thread_local 207 + guard 233-259, registry_availability_message 273, select_registry_scope 291-354 with the legacy rule at 318-328 (legacy_registry_endpoint or host:port, key.connection == "default"), .expect at 317. RegistryTarget is in storage/show_workspaces.rs:19, so RegistryTarget::legacy_source(&AppConfig) there is boundary-correct (storage may read storage::config).

findings.title: Pure journal-confirmation logic is only tested through subprocess, file system and GTK main-loop tests
findings.evidence: confirm_registry_through, confirm_registry_target_through and the take_while(succeeded) successor rule in registry_write_finished (83-120) are pure BTreeMap logic. Every test (e.g. 597, 701, 774, 823, 884, 936) runs through background_io::isolated_test_child (a spawned subprocess with a 30 s deadline), real temp files and glib::MainLoop drains.
findings.recommendation: Extract `pub(crate) struct RegistryJournal { revision, operations: BTreeMap<u64, Op>, failures, error, retrying }` into src/ui/persist/registry_journal.rs. Give it methods admit(target, write) -> u64, finished(revision, covers_snapshot, Result) -> Option<FailureTicket>, begin_retry() -> Option<RetryBatch>, finish_retry(revision, ok, failure_count) and status() -> RegistrySaveStatus. Write 6-10 fast unit tests: per-target confirmation, a failed predecessor holding back successful successors, a retry resolving only its own failures. Keep the existing isolated tests as integration coverage.
findings.risk: Slow, flaky-prone coverage for the logic that protects against data loss. Regressions get noticed late.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: confirm_* 69-81 and registry_write_finished 83-120 are BTreeMap logic; persist.rs uses background_io::isolated_test_child 6 times; isolated_test_child (background_io.rs:379-) re-execs the test binary. Extraction to a pure RegistryJournal is sound.

findings.title: Each background job runs a 20 ms polling timer and an unbounded thread; config lock uses expect
findings.evidence: run() calls std::thread::spawn for every job (106) and deliver_on_main_thread adds a glib::timeout_add_local(20ms) per job (356). run_config_snapshot adds another 20 ms timer per batch (220), and flush_pending adds a third (324). N in-flight jobs means N wakeups at 50 Hz. The config slot uses `slot.lock().expect("config snapshot lock")` five times (164, 183, 187, 199, 221). A poisoned lock (e.g. a panic while it is held) panics the GTK thread inside the timer. The file also mixes four concerns: spawn and deliver, FIFO lanes (13-85, 121-138), config coalescing (140-243) and the failure ledger and close barrier (245-345).
findings.recommendation: (1) Replace the poll loop with a wake-up: deliver through `glib::MainContext::default().spawn_local(async move { let v = rx.recv().await; ... })` using an async oneshot (futures_util::channel::oneshot is already a dependency via futures_util), or use `gio::spawn_blocking(work).await` inside spawn_local for run() (pattern already used in global_shortcuts/portal.rs:68). (2) Use `lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)` for ConfigBatch, since the data is a plain flag and slot. (3) Split the file per proposed_splits. Keep the panic-to-Disconnected semantics: a dropped oneshot sender gives Canceled, which maps to record_failure().
findings.risk: Idle CPU wakeups grow with pending I/O. A lock poisoning becomes a crash on the UI thread.
findings.verifier_note: Polling confirmed: thread::spawn per job 106, 20 ms timers at 220, 324, 356. Lock claim overstated: only 199 and 221 run on the GTK thread; 164, 183, 187 run on the serial Config worker. The lock is never held while user work runs (work is taken out at 164-178 and catch_unwind wraps it outside the guard), so poisoning is practically unreachable - downgrade the lock part to low; unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner) is still a fine hardening. Delivery rewrite correction: futures-util is declared as plain "0.3" (Cargo.toml:21); futures_util::channel needs the `channel` feature, which I did not verify is enabled - either enable it explicitly or use futures-channel/async-channel. gio::spawn_blocking only fits run(); run_serialized jobs execute on dedicated lane threads (background_io.rs:38) and still need a oneshot back to spawn_local.

findings.title: theme.rs mixes theme catalog, CSS security policy, provider registry, desktop integration and motion generation (60% of the file is tests)
findings.evidence: Production (~615 lines) holds: eight thread_local globals (15-24); the BuiltInTheme catalog and localization (42-96, 529-614); the ThemeManager orchestration (128-275); the custom-CSS security validator using cssparser (277-307); generation-guarded async reads (309-318); desktop signal and native color-scheme/motion overrides (320-398); motion CSS generation (400-451); effective_variant (463-475); CSS provider install and clear (477-527). Tests (616-1553) mix base-stylesheet string assertions, WCAG contrast math (1487-1552), native GTK pixel sampling (1154-1348) and validator cases.
findings.recommendation: Split into src/ui/theme/{mod.rs, catalog.rs, custom_css.rs, providers.rs, desktop.rs, motion.rs} plus tests in theme/{contrast_tests.rs, stylesheet_tests.rs, native_tests.rs} (see proposed_splits). custom_css::validate is the trust-boundary check for user CSS. Keep it pure and fully unit-tested, and keep the second check at install time (apply_with_custom_css 245-254).
findings.risk: A change to motion or desktop handling risks the security validator through shared globals, and changes get reviewed in a file mostly made of tests.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: 8 thread_locals 14-24, catalog 42-96 and 529-614, validator 279-307, desktop 320-398, motion 434-451, providers 477-527, tests from 616 (~60% of the file). Line 277 vs 279 is a doc-comment offset, harmless.

findings.title: Adding a built-in theme takes four separate edits; English name/description fields are dead fallbacks
findings.evidence: BuiltInTheme carries name and description (English) that are only reached through the `_ =>` arms of localized_name (60-76) and localized_description (79-95). Both matches list the same 12 id literals already in BUILT_IN_THEMES (529-614). A new theme needs: an array entry, a match arm in localized_name, a match arm in localized_description, plus FTL keys in every locale.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fields with function pointers so the fl! literal checks stay at compile time: `pub(crate) struct BuiltInTheme { id: &'static str, name: fn() -> String, description: fn() -> String, light_css, dark_css }`, each entry `name: || fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "theme-nord-name")`. Delete localized_name/localized_description and the English fields, so callers use `(theme.name)()`. Add a test that ids are unique. CLAUDE.md 'New built-in theme' then becomes a single edit plus CSS and FTL.
findings.risk: A theme added without match arms silently shows untranslated English. Shotgun Surgery.
findings.smell: Shotgun Surgery / Dead Code / Switch Statements
findings.verifier_note: Verified: localized_name 60-76 and localized_description 79-95 duplicate the 12 ids with `_ =>` English fallbacks; name/description fields are read nowhere else in src/ui (grep). Non-capturing closures coerce to fn pointers inside the const array, and fl! keeps compile-time key checks, so the fn-pointer design works. Keep #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)] (fn pointers satisfy all three).

findings.title: Cairo charts and meters hard-code colours, bypassing theme tokens (High Contrast cannot reach them)
findings.evidence: chart::Severity::color returns fixed RGB values (Good = Color(0.20,0.60,0.95) blue; Warning, Critical and Unknown also fixed). Palette::for_current_theme switches between two hard-coded sets on adw::StyleManager::is_dark (96-119). volume_meter hard-codes NOMINAL/WARNING/ERROR bright and dim tuples (65-70) and neutral() black/white ink (401-404). Themes define @scenedeck_success/@scenedeck_warning/@scenedeck_error and are contrast-tested (theme.rs:1440-1485), but these widgets never read them. 'Good' is blue in charts and green (@scenedeck_success) everywhere else.
findings.recommendation: Add src/ui/theme/tokens.rs. It gives `ThemeColors { fg, muted_fg, success, warning, error, accent, surface, border }`, parsed once from the active theme's @define-color lines on apply (parse_theme_colors already exists in tests at theme.rs:1487; promote it to production with error handling) and kept in a thread_local snapshot together with ACTIVE_PREFERENCE. chart::Palette::for_current_theme() and volume_meter::zone_rgba read ThemeColors::current(). Map Severity::Good to success. Keep the meter's dim variants as alpha on the token. Extend the contrast tests to cover chart tokens on scenedeck_card.
findings.risk: Inconsistent meaning of colour. Users of the High Contrast theme get the low-contrast default meter and chart colours.
findings.verifier_note: Chart part confirmed: chart.rs Severity::color 76-81 (Good = blue 0.20,0.60,0.95) and Palette::for_current_theme 96-119 keyed on is_dark. Volume meter part REFUTED: volume_meter.rs:60-64 documents a deliberate decision that zone colours stay fixed to match OBS meter semantics ('a theme that recoloured them would be lying about the level'). Keep meter zones fixed; at most route neutral() ink (401-404) through fg tokens. Restrict tokens.rs consumers to chart.rs.

findings.title: Audio preset Editor is an 18-field god struct with a 180-line render(); preset rules live in the UI
findings.evidence: Editor holds 18 fields (95-116): widgets, baseline, selection, review plan and flags. render() (284-465) computes enablement for 6 buttons, a 6-branch status ladder, results text, row captions, the save label, preview text and save-status notice, and re-runs every 250 ms (699). Preset rules are written in the UI: snapshot() (44-66), review_matches (135-144), save validation (name validity, uniqueness, PRESET_LIMIT; 240-244) and plan construction (483-497). value() re-implements dB formatting with 20*log10 (81-86) instead of services::audio_service::AudioService::format_db. `next.insert(name.clone(), preset.unwrap())` (249) depends on an earlier guard.
findings.recommendation: Domain: add `PresetLibrary` (wrapping BTreeMap<String, AudioPreset>) to src/domain/audio_preset.rs with `save(name, inputs, replacing: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), PresetError>`, `rename`, `delete`, and `plan(name, inputs, epoch, scope) -> Option<PresetPlan>`. Also add `PresetPlan::still_matches(&[PresetInput])`. UI: split into src/ui/audio_presets/{mod.rs (show/wiring), editor.rs (Editor actions), view.rs (render_actions, render_rows, render_preview, render_notice, each <40 lines)}. Use AudioService::format_db. Replace the unwrap with `let Some(preset) = preset else { ... }`.
findings.risk: Preset safety rules (the review-then-apply guarantee) are only testable through GTK, and dB text can disagree with the mixer.

findings.title: Dialogs and widgets redraw on fixed 250 ms or 1 s timers instead of on state changes
findings.evidence: The binding manager and editor rebuild items every 250 ms. Each tick calls action_catalog::binding_entry per binding, and each call clones the input list via inputs(state) (action_catalog.rs:524) and runs fl! lookups (232-247). global_shortcuts::controls, audio_presets::show and output_results_tray poll the same way. operating_panel runs two separate 1 s timers that each walk the full widget tree (107, 118). ui/ has 12+ such 250 ms pollers.
findings.recommendation: Add an AppState change signal. Either a monotonically increasing `AppState::revision: u64` bumped by window.rs after each applied AppEvent and each local mutation, so pollers early-return when the revision is unchanged (a cheap first step), or a `NavigationContext::connect_state_changed(Fn())` that window.rs fires once per drained event batch (event_pump.rs) and pages call instead of glib::timeout_add_local. Merge operating_panel's two timers into one tick. Keep a 1 s tick only where elapsed-time labels need it (sources-status-age).
findings.risk: Constant CPU wakeups and string building while dialogs are open, on a live-production machine.
findings.verifier_note: Verified 250 ms timers at action_shortcuts.rs:367, 551, global_shortcuts.rs:399, audio_presets.rs:699, output_results_tray.rs:25; grep finds 23 250 ms timers in src/ui (non-test). operating_panel has two separate 1 s timers (107, 118). binding_entry calls inputs(state) which clones the catalog (action_catalog.rs:35-43, 524). The revision/state-changed signal is owned by the window.rs/state.rs reviewer - coordinate.

findings.title: D-Bus portal client lives in ui/; raw English errors reach the user; 143-line start()
findings.evidence: portal.rs is a gio-only XDG GlobalShortcuts client with no widgets (BUS/PATH/INTERFACE consts, OwnedConnection, RemoteHandle, Session). It is infrastructure. start() (164-307) nests an async operation with an event-listener closure (203-255), a watchdog and abort handling. Errors are plain English strings: map_err(|_| "Portal connection timed out".to_string()) (197) and portal.rs returning "GlobalShortcuts portal is unavailable". They are shown via `manager.status = format!("{}\n{error}", fl!(..."global-unavailable"))` (303), which breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that all user-facing strings go through fl!. specs() uses three .expect calls on serialization and checksum (68, 79, 81).
findings.recommendation: Move portal.rs to src/infra/portal/global_shortcuts.rs (first check that src/architecture_tests.rs allows gio in infra) with `pub enum PortalError { Timeout, Unavailable, Bus(String), Denied }`. Map it to fl! keys (global-error-timeout, etc., added to every locale) in ui/global_shortcuts/status.rs, and log the raw detail with tracing only. Split start() into session.rs: `async fn run_session(ctx: Rc<Context>, entries: Vec<Spec>) -> Result<(), PortalError>` plus `fn handle_event(ctx, entries, state, event)`. Move the stable-id derivation in specs() (66-81) into a pure `fn shortcut_id(connection, scope, action) -> Option<String>` that returns None on serialization failure.
findings.risk: Untranslated error text, infrastructure code inside the UI module, and a panic path on a GTK future.
findings.verifier_note: English error strings confirmed (global_shortcuts.rs:197, portal.rs:119, 121, map_err(to_string) at 73/82/113/184/240) and surfaced at 303. architecture_tests restricts only domain/services/controller/storage/obs; infra has no gio ban, so moving portal.rs to src/infra/portal/ is allowed. The three expects (68, 79, 81) are effectively infallible (serde of a derived enum, SHA256 always available) - low risk, keep the fix but rank it low.

findings.title: Theme family names contradict their variants; themes differ only in accent and surfaces
findings.evidence: The 'SceneDeck Dark', 'SceneDeck Light' and 'Solarized Dark' families each ship a light and a dark variant (scenedeck-dark-light.css, scenedeck-light-dark.css, solarized-dark-light.css). A diff across resources/themes shows program, preview and image_scrim identical in all 12 dark variants and scenedeck_fg identical in 10 of 12. findings.recommendation: Rename the families to mode-neutral names (e.g. 'SceneDeck Console', 'SceneDeck Paper', 'Solarized'). Keep the old ids as aliases in domain::appearance::ThemeId parsing so saved configs keep working, and add a migration test. findings.risk: Users get confused (a 'Light' theme rendering dark), and editing 24 files to change one shared token.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed variants follow mode, not family name: scenedeck-light-dark.css defines scenedeck_fg #f4f4f4 (dark palette) and scenedeck-dark-light.css scenedeck_fg #1d242e (light palette); solarized-dark-light.css likewise.
